messages:
incident-bot: HIGH severity alert — KV cache size growth + continuous-batching queue depth rising on cluster prod-serving-3. metric: kv_cache_items_total x10 in 5m, batch_queue_depth > 400, tail p99 gen latency 1.9s. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/kv-cache

bob: oncall-sre here, acked. paging @alice @dinesh @carla. attaching initial logs and where I'm looking.

alice: looking — reproduction on prod-serving-3. seeing steady increase in resident memory and a lot of "kv_evict_failed: no eligible pages" in logs. pack sizes jumped suddenly, lots of long-request packs (seq_len > 2048) monopolizing batch slots.

alice: sample log snippet:
```
[14:03:12] pod=svc-prod-3 i-0abc123 :: batch_pack(size=128) latency=45ms requests=[r1(3000), r2(2900), r3(2800), ...]
[14:03:13] pod=svc-prod-3 :: kv_cache.items=1_234_567 kv_evictions=0
[14:03:15] pod=svc-prod-3 :: pagefault spike, background paging overwhelmed
```

dinesh: I rolled the new packing heuristic (pack-mix-v2, commit f8e1b2) last night at ~02:30 UTC. It changes pack scoring to prefer fill-factor over latency — might explain long-request dominance.

carla: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) flip pack heuristic flag to conservative, 2) reduce max_pack_size to 32, 3) enable kv-prefetch throttle, 4) add a quick canary rollback of pack-mix-v2. We can apply flags via Runtime Admin API.

alice: trying conservative flip now (targeting prod-serving-3). curl to admin endpoint:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/runtime/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"pack_heuristic":"conservative","max_pack_size":32}'
```

alice: API resp: 200 OK — applied to region us-west-2 cluster prod-serving-3. rolling config push to 12 pods.

eva: oncall-ml — monitoring. initial signals: batch_pack_max dropped from ~120 to 32, kv_cache growth rate decelerated. p95 gen latency stable, p99 trending down but still elevated for some tenants.

bob: good. any customer impact numbers?

support-bot: 3 escalations opened in last 12m referencing increased embedding latency and occasional 502s. customers: cust-eta, cust-kappa, cust-omega. Support Slack thread: https://slack.internal/support/threads/8753

dinesh: even with pack size reduced, scheduler fairness still skewing — mixed short (seq < 64) requests are getting starved because long requests are still occupying KV cache shards and continuous batching pipeline reuses KVs aggressively. We should enable "fair-slicing" slicing policy and restrict KV prefix cache retention for long sequences.

carla: can flip fair-slicing flag now as a next step. note: fair-slicing increases CPU overhead slightly but should restore short-request tail latency.

alice: applying fair-slicing = true and kv_prefetch_window = 0.2 (reduced). command:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/runtime/config" -d '{"fair_slicing":true,"kv_prefetch_window":0.2}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

alice: resp 200. rolling restarts scheduled to pick up new runtime behavior (batcher picks up config without full restart but kv-layer needs warm restart for eviction policy). starting 4 parallel restarts to avoid capacity cliff.

bob: monitoring telemetry: within 4 minutes after fair-slicing turn-on, short-request p99 decreased from 1.8s -> 220ms on canary pods. overall KV items reduced by ~40% in affected pods. memory pressure falling.

eva: important note — some tenants with long-seq workloads will see throughput drop ~10-15% until we land smarter packing or dedicate capacity. will flag for SRE and account execs.

support-bot: posting a customer advisory draft: "We observed degraded embedding latency in the US-West region due to internal batching heuristics. We are rolling mitigations and expect improved latency within 1 hour. If you continue to see issues, please reply with request IDs." @carla can you review?

carla: LGTM — add ETA 60m and link to status page.

alice: after restarts and config flips, observed side-effect: a small spike in 5xx for long requests (KV eviction thrash during warmup). rolling patch: throttle long-request concurrency on affected pods using route-level limiter (set max_concurrency_long=4). Applying now.

alice: limiter applied via routing API: 200 OK. immediate reduction in 5xx.

dinesh: next medium-term actions: - revert pack-mix-v2 in next deploy if improvements hold - add unit tests for pack fairness with synthetic mixed-workload scenarios - add an autoscale rule that detects pack-size runaway and flips conservative mode automatically.

bob: creating incident ticket and linking customers. incident-bot: please create ticket.

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-0457 created, severity=high. Pager duty: created handoff checklist, assign to oncall-sre night shift.

alice: handoff to night oncall (bob). Summary: initial cause is pack-mix-v2 heuristic causing unbounded long-request packing -> KV cache blowup -> continuous batching pressure -> tail latency for short requests and customer escalations. Mitigations applied: conservative pack heuristic, max_pack_size=32, fair_slicing enabled, kv_prefetch_window reduced, route limiter for long-requests. Monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/incident/INC-2026-0457. Next immediate tasks: watch p99 short-request latency, validate long-request throughput SLA impacts, prepare rollback plan for pack-mix-v2 if needed.

eva: I'm running a canary for a model-dedicated pool for long-seq traffic to reduce impact; will report back in 30m.

bob: ack. I'll own the follow-ups overnight and coordinate postmortem write-up. Assigning action items: alice (hotfix changes + rollback PR), dinesh (fairness e2e tests), carla (customer comms + status page), eva (canary & metrics).

carla: closing immediate channel for noisy alerts; re-open if we see regressions. :lock: :white_check_mark:
